policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'with his horses' is plural, rendering the qere בסוסיו; the ketiv בסוסו is singular 'his horse', which the English wording excludes.
ASV text reads 'Abanah', which is the ketiv אבנה; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Amanah' names the qere אמנה as the alternative the ASV did not follow in its text.
ASV 'Jehovah pardon thy servant' carries no 'I pray thee'/'now', but the ASV does not always render the particle נא, so its absence does not exclude the ketiv; the qere omission is the base fallback.

ASV 'Whence comest thou' is the sense of both the qere מאין and the defectively written ketiv מאן; the variant is orthographic and the English cannot distinguish them, so the qere base fallback stands.
